name: Food waste
description: Edible food is lost or thrown away across retail, food service and households while people go hungry.
solution_summary: Forecast demand and spoilage to cut over-ordering, and match surplus food to food banks and people in real time.

datasets.name: UNEP Food Waste Index Report 2024
datasets.description: Country estimates of household, food-service and retail food waste.
datasets.role: Baseline: how much is wasted, where, and at which stage.

interventions.name: Too Good To Go surplus-food app
interventions.notes: App, not AI: sells surplus food at a discount.

interventions.name: Winnow Vision
interventions.effect: Typical 40–70% kitchen waste reduction, average about 50%
interventions.notes: Camera over the bin identifies discarded food; Winnow Track is the non-AI touchscreen version.

interventions.name: French law against food waste (Garot law)
interventions.effect: Bans destroying edible unsold food; encourages donation contracts. No measured results found yet.
interventions.notes: First national ban of its kind.

data_gaps.gap: Measured (not modeled) household waste for most countries
data_gaps.why_it_matters: Estimates for countries without studies are extrapolated, so models learn from guesses.
data_gaps.how_to_close: Standardized household waste audits; smart-bin data

data_gaps.why_it_matters: Retail surplus is private, so matching it to food banks can't be trained or evaluated.
data_gaps.how_to_close: Partnerships with grocers; anonymized POS + markdown data

risks.who_could_be_harmed: Small farmers and food banks if forecasting shifts surplus away from donation; low-income shoppers if waste cuts come through price.
risks.dual_use: Demand forecasting also optimizes pricing power.
risks.bias_and_representation: Waste data mostly from rich countries; models may not transfer.
risks.ethics: Who owns retailer data shared with charities, and who is accountable when a predicted surplus doesn't arrive.
risks.morality: Is it right to treat hunger as a logistics problem when food is wasted because the hungry can't pay for it?
risks.devils_advocate: Waste is a price and distribution problem, not a prediction problem. Better forecasts mainly save retailers money, and could mean less surplus is donated.

name: Dangerous climate conditions
description: Heat waves, floods and storms are becoming more frequent and severe, and warnings rarely reach people at the neighborhood scale where harm happens.
solution_summary: Downscale reanalysis and forecast data into street-level heat and flood risk, to drive early warnings and adaptation planning.

datasets.name: Copernicus ERA5 reanalysis
datasets.description: Hourly global reanalysis of weather and climate variables, 1940 to present.
datasets.role: Historical heat and precipitation fields to train and validate downscaling.

interventions.name: Ahmedabad Heat Action Plan
interventions.organization: City of Ahmedabad, with NRDC and the Indian Institute of Public Health
interventions.scale: One city; updated yearly; a model for other Indian city heat plans
interventions.effect: About 1,100 deaths avoided per year (Journal of Environmental and Public Health, as reported by NRDC)
interventions.notes: Early warnings, health-worker training, cooling centers, water and shade. Evidence type from the before/after mortality study; check the paper.

interventions.name: Flood Hub
interventions.effect: Riverine flood forecasts accurate at a 7-day lead time
interventions.notes: Historical outputs open as the GRRR dataset (1981–); model not open source.

data_gaps.why_it_matters: Reanalysis is about 30 km resolution; harm is measured at the block.
data_gaps.how_to_close: Hospital heat-illness records; insurance and 311 flood reports

risks.who_could_be_harmed: People in under-sensored neighborhoods if models are confident where data is thin.
risks.dual_use: Hyperlocal risk maps can feed insurance redlining.
risks.bias_and_representation: Sensor and report density tracks wealth, so poorer areas look safer than they are.
risks.ethics: Who is accountable for a missed warning; consent for using health records.
risks.morality: Is it right to put effort into adapting to harm rather than stopping emissions?
risks.devils_advocate: Adaptation tools can make climate change feel manageable and lower pressure to cut emissions. And warnings don't help people who have nowhere cooler or drier to go.

name: Shelter scarcity
description: Not enough safe, affordable housing: people live in slums, overcrowded homes, or on the street.
solution_summary: Predict where housing shortfalls and evictions are coming, to target prevention, vacant-unit matching and zoning decisions.

datasets.name: Population living in slums (% of urban), UN-Habitat via World Bank WDI
datasets.description: Share of urban residents in slum households (SDG 11.1.1 predecessor).
datasets.role: Global picture of inadequate housing by country over time.

datasets.name: HUD AHAR Point-in-Time homelessness counts
datasets.description: One-night counts of people experiencing homelessness by US Continuum of Care.
datasets.role: US ground truth for homelessness by locality.

interventions.name: Housing First (At Home/Chez Soi trial)
interventions.effect: Housed all of the last 6 months: 62% vs 31% with usual care
interventions.notes: Housing without preconditions; participants had serious mental illness.

interventions.name: Homelessness Prevention Unit (predictive model)
interventions.organization: LA County Dept. of Health Services, California Policy Lab
interventions.effect: 86% kept housing; 71% less likely to enter shelter or outreach within 18 months than similar non-enrolled people
interventions.notes: Model ranks who's most at risk; RCT results expected 2027. Evaluator also built the model.

data_gaps.why_it_matters: Point-in-Time counts are a single night a year and undercount hidden homelessness.
data_gaps.how_to_close: Linked shelter, school and health records with consent

data_gaps.why_it_matters: Not in either dataset, but the most direct leading signal.

risks.who_could_be_harmed: Tenants flagged as high risk; people whose records are linked without consent.
risks.dual_use: An eviction-risk score is also a tenant-screening tool for landlords.
risks.bias_and_representation: Homelessness data undercounts youth, women and people avoiding shelters.
risks.ethics: Consent and privacy for linked records; who sees risk scores.
risks.morality: Is it right to predict someone's housing loss rather than guarantee housing?
risks.devils_advocate: The shortage is a supply problem. A model doesn't build homes; it can only ration scarce ones, and may become a way to screen people out.

name: Lack of a living wage
description: Many full-time jobs pay less than what it costs to live where the worker lives.
solution_summary: Estimate local living-wage gaps by joining cost-of-living and wage data, and show which places, sectors and jobs fall short.

datasets.name: MIT Living Wage Calculator
datasets.license: license required for more than 10 locations
datasets.description: Living wage by family type and location in the US.
datasets.role: US cost-of-living side of the gap.

datasets.name: ILOSTAT wages
datasets.description: International wage statistics by country, sex and sector.
datasets.role: Wage side of the gap, internationally comparable.

interventions.name: Real Living Wage accreditation
interventions.effect: 500,000+ workers got pay rises (Cardiff Business School study)
interventions.notes: Voluntary employer accreditation driven by a campaign. The 500,000 figure is a count from a study the Foundation cites, not a causal effect.

data_gaps.why_it_matters: MIT's data requires a license beyond 10 locations, so a free tool can't redistribute it.
data_gaps.how_to_close: License request; or build an open cost-of-living estimate

data_gaps.why_it_matters: Public wage data is by sector and region, not by employer.

risks.who_could_be_harmed: Workers in flagged sectors if employers respond with automation or cuts.
risks.dual_use: Employers could use the same data to pay exactly the local minimum.
risks.bias_and_representation: Informal work is missing from wage data, so the worst gaps are invisible.
risks.ethics: Licensing and attribution for proprietary wage data; accuracy of public claims about employers.
risks.morality: Whose definition of a decent life sets the living wage?
risks.devils_advocate: Living-wage gaps are well documented already. The bottleneck is political will and bargaining power, which a dashboard doesn't change.
